title: The Hollow Wolf Revisited
premise: Silas Sandoval, a temple scribe bound by debt to the valley where magic cannot follow, has spent her life copying prayers she cannot feel. When a feral child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Silas discovers the girl carries the last living dragon-fire — and that the temple's high priests intend to harvest it to seize power over the realm. Fleeing with the child into a world of warring courts and fading magic, Silas must choose between the loyalty she owes her order and the truth that could either reignite an ancient war or end it forever. In the end, Silas gives her own borrowed years to rekindle the dragon-fire freely given rather than stolen, breaking both her debt and the cycle of corruption, while the child — now speaking plainly — becomes the first mage born in the valley in a thousand years.
about_author: Wren Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval manuscripts before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people trapped by institutions, and the small acts of defiance that set them free.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet her grinding ink in the Temple of Quiet Hours, copying scripture to work off her late mother's debt, forbidden to leave the magic-dead valley. A cold, disciplined chapter establishing her longing and resignation. Emotional beat: quiet ache beneath routine.

chapters.title: A Knock at Vespers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. During evening prayer, a mud-caked child appears at the temple door, speaking a language no one recognizes — except Silas, who realizes she can almost understand it. The priests lock the girl in the reliquary. Emotional beat: wonder cracking through duty.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Kings
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, night visit to the reliquary. The child, Ember, draws a dragon sigil matching one hidden in the temple's oldest restricted codex. High Priest Corvane watches Silas from the shadows. Emotional beat: dread dawning alongside fascination.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He reveals he knows what Ember carries: the last dragon-fire, and offers to erase Silas's debt if she helps 'translate' for the girl. His charm barely conceals menace. Emotional beat: temptation wrapped in kindness.

chapters.title: What the Fire Remembers
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Translating for Ember, Silas learns fragments: dragons were not slain but betrayed by the first temples, their fire stolen to build the priesthood's power. Emotional beat: faith beginning to rot from the inside.

chapters.title: The Harvest Rite
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She discovers the 'translation' is preparation for a rite that will drain Ember's fire, killing her. Silas burns the preparation scrolls — her first open act of rebellion. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Border
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. She flees with Ember through the valley's edge, crossing into a world where magic hums like a live wire. Hunted by temple wardens, they shelter with a disgraced hedge-witch, Maren. Emotional beat: vertigo and fragile hope.

chapters.title: The Court of Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The trio reaches a border city where exiled dragon-blooded nobles recognize Ember's sigil — and want to use her as a weapon against the temples. Emotional beat: allies who may be new captors.

chapters.title: Lord Veyra's Bargain
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The exiled lord offers protection in exchange for Ember's fire to fuel his war of vengeance. Silas refuses; Veyra lets them go — but marks them. Emotional beat: the corruption theme made personal.

chapters.title: Ember Speaks
chapters.summary: Ember's POV, first time. Inside her mind we hear the dragon-memory: the ancient war, the betrayal, and a warning that the fire chooses its bearer — it has chosen Silas. Emotional beat: intimacy and terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Ford
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Temple wardens ambush them at a river crossing; Maren is captured buying their escape. Silas uses a scrap of Ember's fire for the first time, and it answers her too willingly. Emotional beat: grief and fear of her own power.

chapters.title: The Price of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Maren's POV, in a temple cell. Under interrogation, Maren learns Corvane plans to ignite a war between the courts so the terrified kingdoms will hand him absolute authority. Emotional beat: sacrifice hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Two Crowns, One Flame
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Both the royal court and the dragon-blooded exiles summon Silas, each claiming Ember. Caught between armies massing on the plains, Silas realizes every faction wants the same thing: the fire, controlled. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure.

chapters.title: The Confession Codex
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In a ruined archive, Silas finds proof of the original betrayal — her own temple forged the doctrine that justified slaughtering the dragons. She must decide whether truth or loyalty to her order matters more. Emotional beat: the book's central choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Maren's Rope
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas trades the confession codex to Corvane in exchange for Maren's release — then reveals she kept copies. Corvane declares war on the exiles within the hour. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into catastrophe.

chapters.title: Plains of Cinders
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Armies clash as Corvane's wardens battle Veyra's dragon-blooded host, both sides trying to seize Ember. Maren falls covering the retreat. Emotional beat: war's cost made flesh.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Ember's POV. Wounded and hunted, Ember's fire begins to die — and with it, perhaps all magic. She tells Silas the fire can be saved only if someone gives their remaining years freely, as the dragons once did. Emotional beat: tender, devastating intimacy.

chapters.title: Corvane Ascendant
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Atop the temple spire, he prepares a stolen fragment of fire to crown himself god-king, believing power is his by right. His chapters reveal a man who once believed in service. Emotional beat: pity inside horror.

chapters.title: The Giving
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Climax. Silas surrenders her years to Ember's fire — freely given, undoing the original theft — and the rekindled flame sweeps across the battlefield, burning away Corvane's stolen fragment and his ambition with it. Emotional beat: transcendent sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Spire
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Corvane, stripped of power and purpose, faces the ruins of his church; the armies stand down as the fire passes overhead, unowned. Emotional beat: exhausted reckoning.

chapters.title: The Debt Unwritten
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Dying but at peace, Silas returns to the valley, now breathing with faint magic. Ember, speaking plainly at last, holds her hand as the ledgers of the temple burn. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming.

chapters.title: First Mage of the Valley
chapters.summary: Ember's POV, epilogue. A year later, Ember tends Silas's grave and the valley's first new spring, carrying the fire forward not as a weapon but a gift. The last line echoes Silas's earliest copied prayer — finally true. Emotional beat: renewal and quiet promise.
